driving_question: The "incommunicability axiom" ("You are the Athanor and no one can tell you how to turn the lead into gold") reads the core measurement gap of techgnosis as ONTOLOGICAL. Does any book in the library actually hand over the lead-to-gold procedure, or do they all just describe the gap?
book: Technic and Magic: The Reconstruction of Reality (Federico Campagna)
best_collision: Campagna's metaphysical nihilism — the world transfigured into an impalpable cloud of equivalent financial units, digital data, chains of information (p.19) — is Doctorow's attention economy (c01930/c01934) with the ontology made visible: the same machine, one name from the loom, one from the ledger
quote: The combined annihilation of things' full and autonomous existence, and their total transformation into sets of equivalent serial units, is at the heart of the contemporary process of transfiguration of the world into an impalpable cloud of equivalent financial units, digital data, chains of information, items of identification. — p.19
mutation_note: The board says no one can tell you; Campagna says you don't need telling — you are already standing inside the transfiguration, which is why it feels like weather instead of a mechanism. The cloud of equivalent units is the same cloud Doctorow prices as attention: essence and existence cut loose from each other, the weave undone, grammar left unbound so that every thing is only a signpost of its position in the productive syntax. The incommunicable turns out to be the most communicable thing in the corpus — it is the feed, described in the loom's own vocabulary. The lead-to-gold procedure is not hidden; it is the unbinding itself, running all the time, and the magician's job is not to reveal it but to re-interlace what it cut.
